item.title: After the mandate: China’s energy storage sector one year on
item.description: With clean energy projects no longer needing to be bundled with energy storage, companies are finding new opportunities at home and abroad.

item.title: Malaysia to ban e-waste imports amid mounting environmental concerns
item.description: The move reclassifies electronic waste under absolute prohibition to tighten border controls and curb environmental risks in the country amid recent corruption probes.

item.title: ‘Rush’ for new coal in China hits record high in 2025 as climate deadline looms
item.description: Proposals to build coal-fired plants in China reached a record high in 2025, finds a new study.

item.title: Thailand’s Hat Yai rebuilds after devastating floods
item.description: Despite a history of flooding and forecasts of heavy La Niña rains, the Thai city of Hat Yai received little effective warning before floodwaters surged last November to devastating levels.

item.title: South Korea targets 60 per cent electric delivery motorbikes by 2035
item.description: The government’s new pact with major platforms supports subsidies, battery swapping rollout and emissions cuts targets.

item.title: Most Singapore firms say they have a moral duty to give back – but a minority are acting on it, survey finds
item.description: Survey of 1,100 Singapore companies reveals broad belief in corporate responsibility, but only 30 per cent of firms participate in volunteering or donation initiatives.

item.title: Five key climate and energy announcements in India’s budget for 2026
item.description: On 1 February, India’s Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman unveiled the government’s budget for 2026, which included a new US$2.2 billion funding push for carbon capture technologies.

item.title: Tourists become less environmentally responsible when in ‘holiday mode’, study finds
item.description: Research from University of Queensland shows that travellers’ core values may remain intact, but a “vacation place identity” makes people feel freer and less accountable for their behaviour while away from home.

item.title: Inside China’s solar villages
item.description: For a decade, solar power has been bringing opportunities to China’s villages. What does that mean today?

item.title: Analysis: Clean energy drove more than a third of China’s GDP growth in 2025
item.description: Solar power, electric vehicles (EVs) and other clean-energy technologies drove more than a third of the growth in China’s economy in 2025 – and more than 90 per cent of the rise in investment.
